_comment: Every switch and number Seekter runs on. /seekter-init copies this file to profile/settings.json as soon as the disclaimer is accepted, then writes each answer the moment it is given, so a half-finished setup still leaves a valid file. You can also copy it and edit it by hand. A key you leave out falls back to the value here. Facts about you and your own rules live in profile/profile.md. Guardrails are never settings: CAPTCHAs, accounts, passwords, accepting terms, messages, LinkedIn Easy Apply and LinkedIn actions stay rules in the skills. Check the file with `python3 scripts/seekter.py settings --check`.
_title_filters: title_keep = the title families worth opening, as one case-insensitive regex. title_drop = wrong seniority, wrong discipline, and the other industries that share your job title. Both are field-specific: build them from the candidate's target titles, then add false positives as runs reveal them. Worked example for a product designer: keep 'product design|\bux\b|design system|\bdesigner\b', drop 'junior|intern|head of|director|graphic|motion|industrial|mechanical|fpga|pcb|interior|fashion|textile|game artist' (the last eight are other industries whose jobs are also called 'designer').
_same_company_days: One application per company within this many days. Greenhouse lets employers auto-reject further applications to a department inside a window, silently. A live interview or offer holds the company whatever the date. See /seekter-run section 2. 0 keeps only same-day applications on hold; it does not turn the rule off.
_blocked_companies: Companies the candidate never wants to apply to. Names match whole words, not substrings, using the same rule as the same-company check.
_location_flags: Plain phrases that may rule the candidate out given their country and authorization. Flags demote and mark postings; they never delete them. Labels can be wrong, so a flagged posting is still opened, last in its tier.

freehire._categories: freehire's own taxonomy. A discipline is usually spread over several, so query each one. Run `curl -A seekter 'https://freehire.me/api/v1/jobs/facets?q=<target title>'` to see the categories and counts for this candidate's field.

linkedin._mode: email (default): Seekter never opens LinkedIn; it reads the job-alert emails and the links the user brings. read: it also reads searches, the notification feed and job details, read-only, within read_limits, and switches itself back to email at the first warning. Only the user switches read on, after being told it is against LinkedIn's terms. Easy Apply is never filled in either mode. See reference/sources/linkedin.md.
linkedin._searches: One row per title family x location. Each row is a job alert the candidate creates on LinkedIn (Email delivery) and, in read mode, a search Seekter runs. Keywords unquoted (quotes cut recall). location is for the alert; geo_id is for read-mode searches, from the table in reference/sources/linkedin.md (92000000 = Worldwide, 91000002 = EEA). remote = LinkedIn's Remote filter, which hides hybrid and on-site roles, so add a second row without it where the candidate can work on-site. EEA leaves out the UK and Switzerland.

_employers: Companies to watch directly: Seekter reads their public job board API every run, so a posting is seen before any aggregator copies it. One row per company: name, ats (greenhouse, ashby, lever, workable, smartrecruiters or recruitee) and slug, the board's own id (job-boards.greenhouse.io/<slug>, jobs.ashbyhq.com/<slug>, jobs.lever.co/<slug>, apply.workable.com/<slug>, jobs.smartrecruiters.com/<slug>, <slug>.recruitee.com). Pick employers that hire remotely where the candidate lives or sponsor where they would move. Run `python3 scripts/employer_sweep.py`; a wrong slug is reported, not guessed. See reference/sources/direct-employer.md.
_boards: Job boards for this candidate's field, with how often they are worth a visit. reference/sources/_core.md rates the general ones and reference/sources/ has one file per measured board; niche boards are per-discipline, so ask the candidate which they already read.
